issues.legal_issue: Interested eyewitness testimony is not to be rejected solely because the witnesses are interested when the evidence is supported by the circumstances of the attack.
material_facts: The prosecution relied principally on two eyewitnesses whom the courts described as highly interested.
One of the eyewitnesses was an injured survivor.
The witnesses attributed the attack to the accused collectively, and the victims had numerous injuries.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness evidence could not be rejected solely because the witnesses were interested, particularly in view of the number of injuries; the collective allegation was not to be rejected on that ground alone.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that evidence is not necessarily unreliable merely because a witness is interested. It relied on the injured witness's evidence and the number of injuries as supporting circumstances. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was cited for this principle.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The case is an appeal challenging criminal convictions.
predicates.interested_witness_testimony: The prosecution's account of the attack is given by witnesses who have an interest in the case.
predicates.injury_evidence_supports_attack: The victims' injuries are consistent with the witnesses' account that an attack occurred.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction based on interested witnesses and the victims' injuries support their account of an attack, the testimony is not rejected solely because of the witnesses' interest.

issues.legal_issue: An unlawful assembly's common object to cause death, and murder liability based on that object, are not established where the attack and medical evidence do not show an intention to kill or objectively establish injuries sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature.
material_facts: The appellants were convicted of murder with liability based on membership in an unlawful assembly.
The assailants used sharp-edged weapons and sticks, but the injuries to the deceased were principally on the arms and other non-vital parts.
The deceased's injuries included fractured ribs, but the medical evidence disclosed no damage to the heart or lungs and no corresponding external injuries for the rib fractures.
The medical evidence did not objectively establish that any injury was sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature; most injuries were described as simple.
The deceased died from shock and haemorrhage, and the injuries to the other victims were also principally on their arms and legs.
issues.conclusion: The common object to cause death was not established, and the convictions for murder with liability based on the unlawful assembly were set aside. The appellants were instead convicted of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304, Part II read with Section 149, IPC.
issues.legal_principle: The common object of an unlawful assembly must be inferred from circumstances including the nature of the weapons, the force used, and the injuries caused. Under Section 300, clauses 1 and III, IPC, the murder classification was not made out on these facts: there was no demonstrated intention to cause death, and the prosecution had not objectively proved that an injury was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. The court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal_in_assembly_case and unlawful_assembly_attack and injuries_largely_non_vital and not objective_proof_of_fatal_sufficiency and not evidence_of_intent_to_kill

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal_in_assembly_cas: The case is an appeal from a murder conviction based on an accused's membership in an unlawful assembly.
predicates.unlawful_assembly_attack: Members of the assembly attacked the victim together.
predicates.injuries_largely_non_vital: The injuries were principally inflicted on non-vital parts of the victim's body.
predicates.objective_proof_of_fatal_sufficiency: The medical evidence objectively establishes that an injury was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
predicates.evidence_of_intent_to_kill: The circumstances of the attack indicate that the assailants intended to cause death.

issues.definition: If an assembly-based murder conviction is appealed, the assembly attacked together, the injuries were largely non-vital, and the evidence neither objectively establishes an ordinarily fatal injury nor indicates an intention to kill, the murder conviction is reduced to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

issues.legal_issue: The benefit of a ruling reducing murder liability may be extended to co-accused who were convicted in the same case but did not appeal when the same reasoning applies to them.
material_facts: Four co-accused were convicted along with the appellants in the same case but were not before the court in the appeal.
The court determined that the common object to cause death was not established and considered that the four co-accused must receive the same benefit.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside the four co-accused's murder convictions and substituted convictions for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, while confirming their convictions on the other counts.
issues.legal_principle: The court extended the benefit of its conclusion to co-accused not before it because they had been convicted in the same case and the court considered that they must receive the same benefit. No earlier case or separate statutory principle was cited for this step.

rule.if: appellate_review_of_joint_trial and co_accused_did_not_appeal and same_murder_conviction_and_basis and same_reasoning_applies

predicates.appellate_review_of_joint_trial: An appellate court reviews convictions arising from a joint criminal trial.
predicates.co_accused_did_not_appeal: A co-accused convicted in the joint trial did not bring the appeal before the court.
predicates.same_murder_conviction_and_basis: The non-appealing co-accused received the same murder conviction on the same basis as the appellants.
predicates.same_reasoning_applies: The appellate court's reasons for reducing the appellants' murder liability apply equally to the non-appealing co-accused.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a joint trial concerns co-accused who did not appeal but received the same murder conviction on the same basis, and the appellate court's reasoning applies equally to them, the reduction in murder liability is extended to them.
